detail.abstract: Text emotion recognition has grown task by task, so polarity, discrete emotions, interpersonal implicatures such as sarcasm, and continuous affective dimensions are each handled by a separate model. In this article, we construct Affeline, a Late-Read foundation model that learns fifteen text emotion tasks with one set of weights. A frozen large language model is adapted with lowrank modules, and the input places the task channel after the body text, so that under causal masking the body representation is provably independent of the channel while the readout stays conditioned on the task. The readout is the last-layer hidden state at a single read position, and training-size imbalance is handled by uniform task sampling. Across English and Japanese data, the single model is on par overall with same-capacity specialists; its benefit is larger on low-resource tasks and a small cost where data are abundant, a descriptive trend that does not reach significance. The frozen representation transfers to held-out tasks, where a linear probe far exceeds the base model and approaches a dedicated specialist. The label names suffice without an explicit task identifier, and the model is released for research use.

detail.abstract: Generative AI improves performance on individual tasks, but whether those gains translate into firm growth, and for which firms, remains an open question. We study a leading Chinese e-commerce platform that in 2024 embedded a generative AI system in the operating software firms use to run their businesses, drawing on centrally developed models and platform-wide data to deliver ready-to-use applications to every firm. Complete records of each firm's AI use, linked to its monthly operations and sales, let us trace adoption through changes in business capabilities, such as reaching customers and introducing new products, to sales growth. Using a matched difference-indifferences design and focusing on firms with annual sales below RMB 5 million, we find that adoption raises monthly sales by 51.6%, primarily through a 47.0% increase in the number of orders; instrumental-variable estimates confirm these results. Adopters reach more customers, update their product lines faster, and deliver better product and service quality, with the largest proportional gains for the smallest firms. Two mechanisms help explain the results. First, AI lowers the cost of routine work: adopters produce more product content and change listings more often while spending less staff time per order, and the gains are largest for firms that faced the highest costs relative to sales before adoption. Second, AI reduces information frictions: adopters post richer product information, and the gains are largest in markets where demand is hard to predict and matching quality is poor, especially for small firms. At the market level, product categories with greater pre-existing information frictions see more sales by existing firms, more entry, and more new products. AI expands markets rather than merely shifting sales from non-adopters to adopters.

detail.abstract: We study how capital regulation affects green lending when banks differ in both regulatory capacity and green-lending capability. We show that these two attributes are complements across every lending regime created by the capital constraint, so aggregate capital is not a sufficient statistic for green credit: it matters which banks hold it. Holding aggregate equity, aggregate brown exposure, and all marginal distributions fixed, re-matching capability to capacity changes aggregate green lending by 5.7%, in a numerical economy initialized using cross-sectional patterns motivated by EU supervisory data. The same complementarity makes green capital relief a targeting problem: at equal realized capital relief, targeting on regulatory slack alone lowers cumulative green credit by 7.9% relative to uniform relief. Over time, the same complementarity produces a brown trap. Legacy brown loans exhaust regulatory room, capability erodes while green lending is halted, and banks can remain out of green lending after their balance sheets recover. In an illustrative mechanism calibration in which this mechanism operates, a chosen legacy-exposure stress generating a median five-period zero-slack spell leaves 17.5% of exposed simulated banks trapped relative to the no-erosion counterfactual. The green transition is thus a problem of distributional banking dynamics, not only of the behavior of the average bank.

detail.abstract: The legal tradition is a key cause of economic development. To clarify its determinants, we study the first legal orders recorded in Bronze Age Mesopotamia. We build on the idea that, for non-negligible legal decentralization costs, the mix of uncertain case law and discretionary inquisitorial adjudication can prevail over the bundle of certain statute law and bright-line adversarial adjudication only when special interests are favored. This occurs when the political process is sufficiently autocratic and/or legal preferences are sufficiently diverse. Consistent with this intuition, the rising ethnolinguistic diversity of the Akkadian empire pushed the dominated polities to prefer discretionary inquisitorial adjudication by a local court that made the law treating its own and the imperial rulings as binding, to lawmaking by an imperial envoy. The latter would have cared only about transfers. Similarly, the more politically inclusive and culturally homogeneous pre-Akkadian polities and the politically weak and commercially interconnected post-Akkadian kingdoms adopted statute law along with bright-line adversarial adjudication. Our estimates remain stable across identification strategies and notably, when we control for trade-related legal decentralization costs and when we rely on instrumental variables. Specifically, we instrument the division of the decision-making power with the political instability driven by the presence of young kings in neighboring polities and the ethnolinguistic heterogeneity with the climatedriven migration of out-of-sample peoples.

detail.abstract: This paper evaluates a large-scale French program (PACEA) providing intensive job-search assistance and placement into training to unemployed youths. Guided by a job-search and matching model, we combine fine-grained administrative data with an instrumental-variables strategy that exploits the quasi-random assignment of youths to caseworkers and their heterogeneous propensity to enroll youths into the program, identifying the causal impact of participation over a four-year horizon. PACEA raises employment probabilities by about 10% after completion. These gains arise exclusively along the extensive margin and are not accompanied by higher wages, contract stability, or occupational upgrading. Analysis of mechanisms points to intensified interactions with caseworkers, more structured job-search trajectories, and short vocational training. Bringing the model to the data, we document negative spillovers on non-participants and highlight the importance of labor demand and program design for achieving higher aggregate employment gains and more favorable benefits-costs ratios.

detail.abstract: Despite abundant literature highlighting the necessity of using non-affine option pricing models to correctly replicate observed market prices, research has predominantly focused on affine models due to their mathematical and computational tractability. Such models employ the Heston model as a building block and add stylized features (e.g., jumps) to improve empirical performance. In this paper, we suggest a different model as a benchmark, i.e., the Extended Hull-White (EHW) model. This belongs to the class of polynomial models and presents a priori more realistic stylized features than Heston, such as non-perfectly correlated moment dynamics, stochastic central tendency and stochastic volatility of volatility. Unlike well-studied affine models, polynomial processes lack efficient estimation methods combining returns and derivatives data. Therefore, we propose a quasi-Bayesian estimation framework for general polynomial pricing models, enabling parameter inference under both risk-neutral and physical measures. Notably, the computing time is smaller than that required for estimating affine models, eliminating their traditional computational advantage. We find that EHW (and most of its special cases) perform better than Heston in-and out-of-sample, and provide a financial explanation. More specifically, we find that EHW presents more realistic trajectories of important quantities such as the conditional leverage path and variance of variance, leading to improved higher-order moment dynamics and related risk premia.

detail.abstract: A single threshold above the poverty line offers an appealing way to classify households as poor, vulnerable, or economically secure. This paper shows that, when vulnerability is defined as expected poverty, applying a common vulnerability threshold to observed consumption faces two problems. First, a vulnerability threshold may lie below the poverty line or may not exist. Second, households with the same current consumption may face very different risks of future poverty, implying household-specific vulnerability thresholds. We establish necessary and sufficient conditions for the existence of these thresholds and show that applying appropriate risk deflators to household consumption allows a common vulnerability threshold to be used on the risk-adjusted consumption scale. We then discuss three approaches to setting this common threshold and examine the consequences of leaving consumption unadjusted for risk. In our Malawi illustration for 2024-25, failing to adjust consumption for household-specific risks leads to the misclassification of 16-22 percent of the population.

detail.abstract: Scientific misconduct in the medical and health sciences remains a major concern for practitioners, patients, scientists, and funders. Even as retractions of fraudulent articles have increased sharply in recent years, concerns remain that detected cases represent only the tip of the iceberg and that actual prevalence of misconduct in the scientific system may be much higher. In this study, we estimate the size of the hidden population of scientists associated with articles that have been retracted for severe misconduct by applying capturerecapture methods. Distinguishing first authors and last authors associated with retracted articles, we find a capture rate of approximately 23% and a population of around 4,250 first authors associated with articles that have been retracted due to severe misconduct in the medical and health sciences. Among last authors, we find a capture rate of 34% and a population of around 4,125 scientists. Our results imply that most fraud in the medical and health sciences remains undetected, yet suggest that only a small fraction of the scientific workforce is associated with articles affected by severe scientific misconduct.

detail.abstract: This study examines the causal impact of state-level Paid Family Leave (PFL) policies on sleep duration and labor market outcomes in the United States. Leveraging the staggered implementation of PFL across states between 1998 and 2020, I employ a staggered difference-indifferences design using the Current Population Survey (CPS) and the American Time Use Survey (ATUS). The CPS is used to estimate the impact of PFL on employment, labor force participation, and hours worked per week while ATUS data assess the effect on sleep duration. Results show that PFL increases employment and working hours, with stronger effects among married men. For women, the impact varies by marital status: single and divorced women increase their labor force participation and working hours, While married women show no significant change, this may suggest that women were able to utilize the available leave program and subsequently return to their jobs. However, married men respond by increasing their own labor supply, suggesting a compensatory household labor adjustment. In addition, sleep duration improves slightly, particularly for women and single individuals. These findings suggest that PFL policies support labor market attachment while offering benefits to personal well-being and enabling families to adapt caregiving responsibilities without withdrawing from the workforce.

detail.abstract: Successive assessments of a manuscript can share errors when reviewers draw on overlapping evidence or similar AI assistance. We study how dependence between assessments affects investment in quality and the value of committing to less dependent reassessment, holding each score’s distribution conditional on quality fixed. More independent reassessment can weaken investment incentives at fixed cutoffs. Under a binding quota, the incentive effect depends on the quality of projects helped by reassessment relative to those displaced by a tighter cutoff. Under posterior ranking, its sign is the difference in the value of the two sources’ information after rejection at the same marginal threshold. With normal scores, lower correlation gives a strictly positive effect at a fixed pool. The investment response creates a difference in the value of acquiring information before and after investment. With selective reapplication, an interval of unit costs yields positive reassessment under commitment and zero reassessment in a discretionary equilibrium.

detail.abstract: We propose a directional tail-based stock-selection method using conditional return distributions to examine how distributional information revealed by machine learning prediction models can be translated into investment value for long-short portfolios, and why this value may persist despite arbitrage competition. Existing research on machine learning asset pricing primarily focuses on conditional mean prediction. Although recent studies incorporate quantiles, predictive probabilities, and uncertainty information, they have not fully established how different parts of the return distribution should inform long and short decisions separately, or how the incremental value of distributional information arises through portfolio returns and joint risk. To address these limitations, we aggregate quantile endpoints calibrated using historical errors across multiple coverage levels to construct separate upperand lower-tail measures, and combine them with the cross-sectional ranks of point forecasts to form directional stock-selection signals. In a sample of U.S. stocks from 1992 to 2024, the method increases full-sample gross Sharpe ratios for both equal-and value-weighted portfolios across ten machine learning prediction models: the model averages rise from 2.411 to 2.781 and from 0.902 to 1.251, respectively. Further leg-level analysis shows that improvements in equal-weighted portfolios arise primarily from covariance-based risk offsets between the long and short legs, whereas improvements in value-weighted portfolios more strongly reflect the combined effects of directional returns and risk matching. Our economic mechanism analysis finds that the method jointly uses conventional return characteristics and information related to idiosyncratic volatility, liquidity, and trading frictions, linking directional selection of high-risk stocks to overall portfolio risk management. Realizing these investment opportunities often requires specialized resources, including securities-lending supply, financing capacity, risk capital, and trade execution capabilities. Thus, even when market participants can identify the relevant return information, implementation constraints may limit the speed with which arbitrage capital eliminates its investment value. These findings reveal the portfolio decision value of conditional return distributions and provide new empirical evidence on return predictability and limits to arbitrage in machine learning asset pricing.

detail.abstract: We examine how investors' reactions to proposed flexibility in mandatory reporting frequency vary with firms' pre-existing voluntary disclosure practices. Using three U.S. policy events during 2025-2026, we compare firms with established quarterly management guidance practices with firms that provide guidance only at an annual horizon. Annual-only guiders experience announcement returns approximately 100 basis points lower than quarterly guiders. The difference is negative around each event, persists across alternative definitions and measurement windows for quarterly guidance, and is unusually large relative to return differentials observed on placebo dates. Because the proposed regime has not yet been implemented, these reactions reflect investors' expectations about firms' reporting choices and their consequences. Overall, our findings suggest that investors' assessments of reporting-frequency flexibility depend on firms' established voluntary disclosure practices.

detail.abstract: The accelerating decarbonization of the global economy is transforming the relationship between international trade and climate governance. Yet the legal frameworks governing these domains remain fragmented, producing tensions between economic integration, climate ambition, and regulatory sovereignty. This article examines how states can reconcile trade liberalization with decarbonization without assuming that a single regulatory model is universally transferable. Through a comparative analysis of the European Union, the United States, South Africa, and Saudi Arabia, it demonstrates that contemporary approaches to decarbonizing trade reflect distinct combinations of carbon regulation, industrial policy, trade measures, and institutional governance. The analysis shows that legal fragmentation is not merely an obstacle to climate action: under certain conditions, it can permit differentiated and context-sensitive regulatory experimentation, while under others it can generate regulatory conflict, competitive distortions, and implementation gaps. The article develops a framework of adaptive climate-trade governance, under which jurisdictions combine common principles of carbon accounting, transparency, and regulatory coordination with differentiated instruments reflecting their economic structures, institutional capacities, and political constraints. The comparative analysis further demonstrates the importance of sequencing. The European Union's emphasis on carbon accounting, monitoring, and border adjustment, the United States' use of targeted industrial incentives, and South Africa's experience with phased carbon regulation illustrate different pathways toward trade-compatible decarbonization. Saudi Arabia provides a particularly important case of selective adaptation, demonstrating how a hydrocarbon-dependent economy can pursue decarbonization through a functionally differentiated framework rather than institutional transplantation. The article argues that the future of decarbonizing trade lies not in eliminating legal diversity, but in governing it through interoperable rules, credible carbon measurement, coordinated institutions, and progressively aligned climate-trade policies.

detail.abstract: Falling technology costs are making solar PV the dominant source of renewable capacity growth and central to achieving net-zero emissions. Yet utility-scale solar's substantial land requirements place it in direct competition with agriculture. Exploiting China's unprecedented prioritization of food security after 2012 as an exogenous shock, we find that high-yield counties experienced an 11.2-percentage-point decline in new-deployment probability, nearly half the sample mean, and a 0.122 km 2 decline in annual PV area, equal to average annual county deployment, relative to low-yield counties. Moreover, the policy appears to overshoot: its effects extend to non-cropland and nearby low-yield counties and are no stronger in counties highly productive in China's most import-dependent staple crop. Mechanism evidence points to top-down enforcement rather than voluntary local adjustment, with restrictions on county governments' land conveyance to PV developers as the potential channel. Under highly conservative assumptions, we estimate forgone annual CO 2 abatement of 9.2-14.3 million tons, while finding no measurable increases in grain output or cultivated-land area. These findings from the world's largest solar market highlight the food-energy conflict as a substantial barrier to the global energy transition.

detail.abstract: Whether traditional commercial culture can translate into corporate export resilience in the digital era is a key question for understanding the contemporary value of informal institutions. Using a sample of small, medium-sized, and micro listed firms on China's A-share markets from 2008 to 2023, we measure the potential influence of merchant guild culture by the geodesic distance between a firm's registered address and the nearest historical merchant guild origin, and examine its association with export resilience and the moderating role of digital transformation. We document a significant positive association between merchant guild culture and export resilience, which remains stable under propensity score matching and alternative sample scopes. The association is stronger for firms with higher levels of digital transformation and greater director network centrality. Our findings provide empirical evidence on the complementarities among traditional commercial culture, digital capability, and corporate social networks, and offer implications for cultivating open and collaborative business networks that strengthen firms' capacity to withstand external shocks.

detail.abstract: Taxes on wealth, property and estates need current values for assets that rarely trade. Self-assessment takes them from the owner's own choices, but existing designs each give something up. Harberger's tax forces a sale at the declared value and breaks down for jointly owned assets. Levmore's (1982) competitive assessment lets the owner refuse a bid and pay tax on it, but states no rule for values that fall. This paper gives the first self-assessment scheme, to our knowledge, that tests values against the market in both directions, never forces a sale, and works for jointly owned assets. Owners set their own values and have reason to keep them close to the market price, whether it rises or falls; no appraiser is needed. The design rests on a theorem: when side payments and legal entities are free, no rule that reads recorded transactions is collusion-proof, and only the market's refusal of an open offer survives in both directions, because no owner can know in advance everyone able to study the asset. Valuation error falls with asset size, down to what outsiders can know.

detail.abstract: Capital diversification and risk diversification often disagree: equal weighting spreads the budget but not risk, and equal risk contribution spreads risk but not the budget. We measure both on a common scale, the effective number of assets implied by the entropy of weights and of risk contributions, and characterize the capital-risk diversification frontier: the largest capital diversification attainable for each level of risk diversification. The frontier depends only on the covariance matrix and splits the capital concentration of any portfolio into a part imposed by the universe and a part added by the allocation rule. Its fixed point, the highest level that both dimensions can reach simultaneously, measures the diversification capacity of the universe; the Entropy-Balanced Risk Contribution (EBRC) portfolio attains it without any tuning parameter by maximizing the weaker dimension. In euro area government bonds and a multi-asset ETF universe, diversification capacity tracks the dispersion of volatilities, and standard compromise rules can leave more than 10% of the attainable capital diversification unused. Out of sample, EBRC matches or beats the best tuned rule in sovereign bonds, and is slightly worse in the multi-asset universe, although the difference is not robustly significant. The frontier is most useful as a diagnostic, not as an optimizer.

detail.abstract: An Indian investor in a systematic investment plan (SIP) sees units, a net asset value (NAV), a current value and, in factsheets, a return before tax and before inflation. This paper follows a SIP through its whole life cycle to measure what those figures leave out: expenses in rupees, tax at redemption, inflation in each year, what the scheme does between monthly disclosures, and who checks where the money is. Using public data for 254,409 rolling SIPs in 1,179 growth plans of open-ended equity schemes, January 2014 to September 2026, a regular-plan SIP kept at the median about 68% of the gain its statement showed after tax and inflation over ten years, and about 60% for ten-year SIPs ending in September 2026. Median annual returns over ten years fall from 16.0% as a factsheet would show them to 14.8% after tax and 9.5% after inflation. Most long SIPs therefore did gain in real terms in this period, but short ones often did not: 34% of one-year and 9% of five-year regular-plan SIPs lost purchasing power. Inside the NAV, a return gap of +0.049% a month (t = 3.71) arises mostly in months when a scheme holds a newly listed IPO; outside them it is +0.017% (t = 1.49), though +0.024% (t = 2.80) before April 2026. Window dressing was not detected at this sample size. The paper does not rank funds, give advice or allege wrongdoing.

detail.abstract: Vision-language models (VLMs) often read a short video as one image with the frames arranged as panels. To describe a person over time, the model must find the same individual in each frame and report that individual's state. However, it is unknown whether the geometry of such panels changes which person the model reports. In this study, we build a controlled analysis framework for temporal person-state attribution in two-frame panels. Three people rotate by one position between the frames, so another person moves into the target's former image column. The second frame is then shifted horizontally in graded steps, which changes only the column overlap. We also vary the wording that names the target and add visible badges that stay with each person or each position. Separate and joint queries test whether an error replaces only the state or the whole person. We apply the framework to schematic figures and real face photographs and compare six VLMs. In Qwen3-VL-8B, column alignment consistently raised reports of the person who now stood in the target's former column. The error weakened gradually with the shift and was much smaller for side-by-side frames. In joint answers, the model reported the other person's place and state together. Person-fixed badges reduced this error, whereas position-fixed badges increased it sharply. InternVL3.5-14B did not show the alignment effect, but the badges steered it in the same directions. Thus, frame alignment can redirect person-state attribution toward the wrong person, and correspondence cues steer attribution in both models.

detail.abstract: Two Philippine religious organizations raised money from their members on promises framed in the language of faith, and their fates diverged. KAPA Community Ministry International, founded by Joel Apolinario in Surigao del Sur, asked members to "donate" at least ₱10,000 in exchange for a monthly "blessing" or "love gift" of 30 percent for life. The Securities and Exchange Commission estimated that some five million members had placed about ₱50 billion with it. The SEC issued its first advisory in March 2017, a cease-and-desist order in February 2019, and a revocation of KAPA's registration that April, and in December 2023 a regional trial court in Butuan sentenced Apolinario and two incorporators to life imprisonment on eight counts of syndicated estafa. Kabalikat sa Pamamahayag International (KAPI), founded by Daniel Razon, a broadcaster and now the leader of the Members Church of God International (MCGI), promised health insurance protection instead of prosperity. Members paid about ₱1,200 a month to keep MCGI's preaching on its media platforms UNTV and Wish 107.5, a purpose the church called propagation, and were told that the subscription carried health-insurance policy for their families. An MCGI minister explained that insurance policy on video; he is Danilo V. Navales, a director of Breakthrough and Milestones Productions International (BMPI) holding 4.83 percent of its shares. Earlier research found that the KAPI materials identify no conventional insurer, written policy, defined coverage schedule, assigned benefit value, or formal claims mechanism, and on October 22, 2026, the Insurance Commission's Licensing Division confirmed that KAPI is not licensed to transact any insurance business in the Philippines. A former contributor who fell ill found no policy number and no claims office, and was directed to the barangay, the local government, and the Philippine Charity Sweepstakes Office. A former MCGI national treasurer states that KAPI collected as much as ₱1.3 billion in ten years, that none of its roughly 10,000 members received an insurance benefit, and that the surplus beyond broadcasting paid for privately held shares in BMPI, where Razon's 58.33 percent stake is recorded as ₱175 million fully paid, and for companies and a residence in Brazil, where tax authorities later upheld fraud-level penalties against MCGI's founder and his assistant over foreign receipts of unproven origin. MCGI has since removed every mention of KAPI from Razon's official biography, although archived copies of the page preserve it, and no public record explains the source of Razon's ₱175 million stake in BMPI or of his personal wealth, while no KAPI contributor ever became a BMPI shareholder. The essay sets out how KAPI's record maps onto the elements of syndicated estafa, estafa by conversion, and unlicensed insurance, and shows that KAPI's collections from contributors in the United States, paid through American banks, bring the scheme within reach of the U.S. Racketeer Influenced and Corrupt Organizations Act (RICO), whose remedies include the forfeiture of MCGI and BMPI-UNTV assets in North America and the extradition of those charged.

detail.abstract: Under the CAFTA-DR treaty, Costa Rica was obligated to open its mobile, internet, and data telecommunications markets to private competition after more than six decades of state monopoly. Private competitors entered in 2011, but the incumbent operator ICE remained in government hands. Because ICE was never privatized, Costa Rica's liberalization isolates the effect of competition from the effect of ownership. The crosscountry telecommunications literature has rarely been able to make this split. We estimate the causal effect of that liberalization using synthetic difference-indifferences. Liberalization increased mobile subscriptions by 63 per one hundred inhabitants, with a dynamic buildup from near zero at the treatment date to 99 additional subscriptions by the sixth post-treatment year. A secondary analysis of fixed broadband finds a smaller but significant effect of 4 additional subscriptions per hundred. Both results are validated by in-time placebos that return precisely estimated nulls.

detail.abstract: The rapid proliferation of digital gambling platforms and integrated mobile e-wallet ecosystems has dramatically reduced transactional friction, exacerbating risk exposure and financial distress among vulnerable populations, particularly students and young adults. Conventional interventions rely heavily on passive, retrospective self-reporting and manual oversight, proving inadequate against continuous 24/7 digital wagering environments. This paper presents GAMBYTES, a technology-driven management platform designed to bridge critical operational visibility gaps through realtime behavioral tracking and automated risk mitigation. Built upon a robust five-layer multi-tier architecture (User Interface, Backend Routing, Application Services, MySQL Database, and External Services), GAMBYTES integrates a Boolean Session Termination Rule, standardized Financial Management Behavior Scoring (FMBS), dynamic expense categorization (Needs vs. Wants), and automated emergency alert dispatches to family members and clinical administrators. Empirical deployment at the JJ Valderrama Behavioral Management Center (JJVBMC) from September 18 to November 5, 2026, established a complete 100% digital baseline intake for clinical diagnostic tracking. Algorithmic session evaluations successfully flagged consecutive loss patterns and monthly budget deficits in real time. This work formalizes the architectural framework, empirical outcomes, and systemic recommendations necessary to advance proactive digital health interventions for compulsive behaviors.

detail.abstract: Kuhn-Tucker (KT) demand models characterize consumers' budget allocation through the Karush-Kuhn-Tucker conditions of utility maximization. Classical specifications, including quadratic utility, are widely used to study pricing, assortment, and competition, but remain difficult to estimate from consumer data. By contrast, models designed for tractable estimation often impose restrictive assumptions on demand behavior. We address this gap with two results. First, for KT models whose utilities are linear in their coefficients, we establish convexity of maximum-likelihood estimation under Gaussian shocks through an equivalent chance-constrained reformulation. The same reformulation reduces likelihood evaluation to at most one-dimensional integration, regardless of the number of goods, enabling scalable estimation with global optimality guarantees. Second, we show that mixtures of these estimable KT models can approximate a broad class of consumption distributions to arbitrary accuracy across varying budgets, prices, and assortments, including behavior generated by nonconcave utilities. Numerical studies demonstrate estimation with 50 goods, compared with at most 10 goods for conventional methods within the same time limit, and improved empirical fit from richer utility specifications.

detail.abstract: Selection for scarce opportunities, such as school places and research grants, relies on noisy signals of potential, and allocators learn most about the people they admit. This article extends an agent-based model of denatocracy, the allocation of opportunity by potential, to that setting. Each person's effective potential is the product of ability and will; success requires realisation, effective potential multiplied by opportunity, to reach a threshold; opportunity develops potential; and being passed over erodes will. The allocator observes a noisy test, holds Bayesian beliefs updated from the performance of those it admits, and decides both whom to fund and how large a safety margin to give them. A simple result organises the analysis: under Gaussian beliefs, a person funded with a margin of z standard deviations succeeds with probability Φ(z), whoever is selected, so funding estimated need succeeds only half the time. Over 280,000 simulation runs of 10,000 agents yield four further results. First, noise extends the case for broad allocation: equal shares, which need no information, overtake every targeting rule where development is strong and opportunity scarce. Second, a margin of one to one and a half standard deviations raises successes by 36 to 104 per cent over funding estimated need. Third, the standard remedies for learning under uncertainty do not help: optimistic selection adds nothing, while Thompson sampling and funding lotteries lose up to 30 and 78 per cent of successes. Fourth, in contrast with the perfect-information case, mixtures become optimal: when tests are noisy and opportunity develops potential, the best allocator funds more people with smaller margins and keeps a floor of 10 to 20 per cent of the budget for everyone, gaining up to 20 per cent in successes while using top talent better and reducing inequality. Under uncertainty, allocation should be broader, not bolder.

detail.abstract: Social media platforms monetize your attention through personalized, often undisclosed paid content. These platforms' core goal is to keep you active as long as possible, optimizing towards individual engagement with no regard for a shared reality. That optimization is a major contributor to the social fragmentation in our society. Social media platforms constitute a new fifth wave of propaganda, entirely unique and distinct from prior eras, because persuasion rolls out on a mass scale while being individually tailored to each user. detail.abstract: Consumers may use information acquired in one retail setting when evaluating and purchasing related products in another. We examine whether mandatory calorie posting in restaurants influences household grocery purchases. Using NielsenIQ Homescan data around six local mandates and a stacked difference-in-differences design, we compare jurisdictions where posting becomes operative with those that adopt comparable requirements but do not reach sustained implementation. In a complementary randomized experiment with 593 participants, we measure initial underestimation of grocery calories and whether calorie information on a restaurant menu reduces it. We find the clearest evidence of information transfer where initial underestimation is more common and consumers can relate a grocery product directly to a menu item. Both conditions hold for bakery products, for which calories purchased in grocery stores decline by 2.31 calories per person-day (18.7 percent, p = 0.012), whereas categories with little experimental updating show no similar decline. A shift from whole to lower-fat milk, with little change in total milk calories, provides some evidence of inference to a related ingredient. Our findings suggest that information disclosed in restaurants can affect both category demand and the composition of purchases at grocery retailers, which the posting requirement does not cover. Evaluations confined to restaurant transactions may therefore miss part of the response to disclosure.

detail.abstract: Product attributes can reflect concerns on which political views differ. This study examines whether demand for such attributes changes when a market's news environment shifts. We study Sinclair Broadcast Group's entry into 48 local television markets in 2012-2016, a change in ownership associated with more conservative and nationally focused news coverage. The analysis uses NielsenIQ scanner data for ten packaged-goods categories to measure the volume share of products carrying environmental, health, or animal-welfare attributes for which prior work documents higher demand among liberal households. Relative to matched counties in markets Sinclair did not enter, this share grows more slowly after entry and is 0.087 percentage points lower (6.9 percent in a proportional specification). Household panel evidence suggests slower adoption of these products among households without prior purchases, with less consistent responses over time among earlier buyers. Prices and availability do not change detectably, advertising estimates are negative but imprecise, and purchases fall where acquired stations carried no recorded pre-entry advertising for these products. Search interest in the concerns behind the attributes declines, and the purchase response is concentrated in swing and Republican-leaning counties. The findings suggest that the news environment contributes to partisan differences in purchases.

detail.abstract: With a series of controlled lab experiments, we study the detrimental effects of fake positive and fake negative reviews on market dynamics. We find that fake reviews can erode buyers' trust in the marketplace in ways that are difficult to reverse. In particular, markets initially flooded with fake positive reviews may experience persistently low trade volumes, even long after the fake reviews are removed. To understand such "sticky" buyer perceptions, we develop a hidden Markov model of buyers' decisions to purchase from the market or choose an outside option. Our model identifies four latent states reflecting increasing levels of disillusionment with the marketplace, including a critical "market exit" state from which buyers rarely return. Transitions between these states are strongly driven by negative quality experiences, which accumulate fastest in markets flooded with fake positive reviews. Meanwhile, purchasing decisions at any given state are shaped by factors (emission covariates) such as product prices and review valence. Counterfactual simulations from our model suggest that temporary price discounts can help re-engage buyers after the removal of fake positive reviews, whereas such measures appear unnecessary in cases of expunging fake negative reviews.

detail.abstract: Customer segmentation is widely promoted as an important business strategy, with its use documented across diverse sectors, including entertainment, retail, hospitality and travel. Yet grouping customers guarantees neither meaningful insights nor better business decisions, raising the question whether customer segmentation is a necessary business decision. This article offers business owners a quick guide to deciding whether customer segmentation is worth pursuing. It reviews the benefits, the effect of digitalisation and the main limitations, and argues that segmentation is best viewed as a diagnostic tool whose value is context-dependent: it becomes necessary when customers differ in ways that matter to decisions the business can act on, and when the expected benefits justify the costs.

detail.abstract: Large language models are increasingly used as digital twins or synthetic respondents, yet their performance is typically evaluated using average accuracy alone. We argue that this is incomplete because predictions with similar accuracy can differ substantially in how confidently the model has identified the respondent's answer. We introduce calibrated prediction-level uncertainty using conformal prediction and apply the framework to the Twin-2K-500 dataset, covering more than 2,000 U.S. respondents and over 500 survey questions. Comparing eight conformal methods, we find that Regression-to-Classification Conformal Prediction (R2CCP) achieves the target coverage with the smallest prediction sets across GPT-4.1 mini, DeepSeek V4 Flash and GPT-5.1. Accounting for uncertainty changes the assessment of model performance, as the model with the highest accuracy does not produce the narrowest calibrated sets. We then examine persona information and find that richer profiles improve accuracy but do not necessarily reduce uncertainty. Demographics provide the most consistently favorable joint contribution among four types of persona information (including demographics, personality and psychology measures, cognitive abilities, and economic preferences). Finally, combining accuracy and uncertainty reveals a particularly concerning low-accuracy/low-uncertainty group in which models are confidently wrong. Across models, this group is more strongly associated with conservative political orientation, minority religious and racial groups, status seeking, and more severe cognitive errors.

detail.abstract: How does the language of a charitable appeal, whether communicated in a potential donor's native or non-native (but proficient) language, influence monetary donations? Whereas research finds that people behave more morally in their native (vs. non-native) language, eight preregistered experiments (N = 7,447) and one archival analysis (N = 3,142) find that people donate less in response to appeals in their native language. People facing a donation decision need to determine whether and how much to give, with the appropriate action varying across situations. Situational considerations that inform this decision are more accessible in a native language, making donation decisions seem less diagnostic of the self, reducing giving. Consistent with this process, perceived self-diagnosticity mediates the effect of language on donations, and manipulating self-diagnosticity attenuates this effect. Reconciling these findings with prior research, the relationship between language and moral behavior depends on the type of moral decision under consideration: a native language promotes adherence to moral rules when decisions involve moral violations (stealing; lying), but reduces giving for donation decisions, which we refer to as moral aspirations. Beyond advancing theory on language, self-diagnosticity, and moral behavior, this research offers practical guidance to maximize charitable giving when communicating with multilingual audiences.

detail.abstract: Political economy usually treats state intervention and free markets as opposite ends of one line: as the state retreats, economic freedom grows. This paper argues that the relationship between power concentration and individual economic autonomy is instead an inverted U. Autonomy depends on the conditions Adam Smith identified for a working market: many competing suppliers, free entry and exit, informative prices, and no actor able to dictate terms. Concentration of power destroys those conditions whether it sits in the state or in private firms. The paper makes three contributions. First, it sets out the mechanism by which state and private concentration converge on comparable outcomes for the individual. Second, it builds a composite Power Concentration Index (C_total) that measures state and private concentration on one 0–100 scale, using only published data: the IMF Investment and Capital Stock Dataset, V-Dem, the World Bank governance indicators, the ILO, the World Inequality Database, De Loecker and Eeckhout's global markup estimates, national competition-authority market studies, and StatCounter. Third, it applies the index to 12 economies and, in a reduced core form, to 25. The results show three routes to high concentration: home-grown private concentration (United States, 62.0), imported concentration with weak counterweights (Brazil, 60.3), and state concentration (China, 58.9). Economies with enforced gatekeeper rules and strong institutional buffers sit well inside the lowconcentration band (Germany 35.2, Japan 37.3, France 42.1). No economy yet exceeds the critical threshold of 65, but concentration accelerated sharply after 2020 in India, the United States, Indonesia and Pakistan, driven mainly by weaker checks on executive power. The United Kingdom sits inside the low-concentration band because state power is checked and wealth is dispersed, but its market power is close to US levels and its regulatory counterweight is under pressure. Scenario modelling shows that AIdriven labour displacement would accelerate this drift further: a severe shock brings the US crossing of the critical threshold forward by up to four and a half years. Income explains only 12% of the variation in the core index, and after controlling for it the United States and China remain well above their predicted levels. The autonomy consequences are presented as a hypothesis grounded in established evidence on the harms of excessive concentration, with explicit falsification criteria.

title: How God Survived Reason

detail.title: How God Survived Reason

keywords.keywords: Faith and reason; religion and rationality; creator God; consequential God; religious epistemology; Islamic rationalism; European Enlightenment; divine law; religion and social order; prophecy and revelation; atheism; religion and science

detail.abstract:
One central inquiry that has occupied human intellect is whether God is compatible with reason. Several positions exist on this subject. Strong advocates of faith traditions argue that reason is not a valid means of knowing God; therefore, any dialectic between God and reason is unnecessary. Muslim scholars, among other believers, assert that no contradiction exists between God and reason, as God urges humans to use reason. Similarly, science, as a manifestation of reason, does not oppose God. Atheists, however, argue that God is a non-rational invention of human imagination and that a commitment to rationality leaves no place for God. Some atheists see belief in God as a psychological need rooted in inherent and evolutionary human vulnerabilities.

This article examines whether reason can expel God from human consciousness. Three imperative questions about God are central. First is the creation question: Is there a God who created the universe, including humans? Second is the law-and-order question: Does God, as lawgiver and judge, provide a code of conduct for humans to follow, and will humans be judged, rewarded, or punished in this life or another? Third is the providential question: Is God the problem-solver whom nations and individuals can access for relief in adversity?

detail.abstract: This article develops a conversion-oriented framework for explaining when the coordination of power resources generates geopolitical influence in the Middle East. Existing accounts of smart power emphasize the combination of hard-and soft-power instruments, but often leave the mechanisms connecting resource coordination to observable political outcomes underspecified. The article distinguishes resource possession, mobilization, strategic coordination, behavioural conversion, and durability, and advances four conditional propositions concerning objective alignment, cost imposition, network autonomy, and political consolidation. It applies the framework through an episode-centred qualitative analysis of Iran's regional strategy, focusing on its interactions with Israel and the United States and using Turkey and Saudi Arabia as limited contextual contrasts. Evidence is drawn from peer-reviewed scholarship, official documents, and institutional assessments; the 2025 and 2026 confrontations are treated as contested episodes rather than definitive tests of victory. The analysis shows that asymmetric capabilities, geographic leverage, and regional networks can raise adversaries' costs and constrain their options, but do not by themselves establish durable influence. Conversion requires observable behavioural or institutional change and effects that remain sustainable despite countermeasures. The framework contributes mechanisms and empirical tests for distinguishing tactical disruption, coercive leverage, bargaining outcomes, and structural geopolitical change, while identifying where the conversion process can fail.

detail.abstract: Rio de Janeiro's Pacifying Police Units (UPPs), launched in 2008, sought to replace episodic raids on favelas under criminal governance with permanent, proximity-based policing backed by a "social arm". Quasiexperimental evaluations show that early roll-outs reduced homicides, police killings and shootouts, but the gains faded after 2016. Drawing on an original interview with José Mariano Beltrame, Rio's Secretary of Public Security from 2007 to 2016, and on the quantitative and qualitative evaluation literature, this paper argues that the model did not fail because territorial presence cannot work, but because it lacked systemic police reform, a governed social-delivery arm, disciplined scale and protection against fiscal and legitimacy shocks. It proposes a two-tier, 24-36-month package. In a few sites, a "UPP 2.0" combines permanent presence with reform gates, a civilian Social Task Force bound to a 180-day service commitment, consolidation tests and an explicit exit to regular policing. Elsewhere, time-bound "conditional saturation" operations-triggered by published indicators of armed control, such as refuse collection, postal delivery or utility repairs that can no longer reach a neighbourhood-target weapons rather than drug markets and end when services return. Both tiers depend on a leadership shock that removes the officers who drive police corruption and empowers those who resist it. A section added in 2026 examines Operação Contenção-the October 2025 raid on the Alemão and Penha complexes that left 122 people dead-as the opposite of conditional force: maximum lethality without warning, occupation, accountability for the deaths or lasting change in who governs the territory.

detail.abstract: Social media sentiment is increasingly used to predict stock returns. Its reliability depends on the composition of the crowd generating the feed. For foreign firms, the home-market investors who know them best are underrepresented on English-language Twitter. Hence, their feed should carry a less precise signal. Reduced-form analysis of firm-level Twitter sentiment shows that sentiment noise predicts next-quarter losses less consistently for foreign stocks than for domestic stocks. The loss-on-noise slope is negative in 78 percent of quarters for domestic stocks but in only 48 percent for foreign stocks, with a significant mean difference in slopes. We interpret this difference through a noisy rational expectations model in which the feed carries a public signal produced by three types of contributors. Specialists post repeatedly with information about the firm, attention-driven contributors post once with information about the firm and a transient fad, and automated accounts post repeatedly with no information about the firm. The share of each contributor type and the size of the fad determine the precision of the signal, which, in turn, determines how much of the feed's noise reaches prices. The model gives repeat-author share, fad and precision from the vendors aggregate metrics, without account-level data, whereas prior work backs out precision from price informativeness. The structural estimates show that feeds for foreign stocks have a higher share of repeat authors, a larger fad component and a less precise signal. Thus, the foreign signal did not disappear but got diluted.

detail.abstract: Cities seeking to revitalize commercial districts must decide which store categories should fill vacant storefronts and where. These decisions are interconnected: a new store competes for destination demand but also generates trips that may continue to other stores. We develop an estimation-and-optimization framework for allocating vacant storefront capacity across locations and categories. Using device-level smartphone location data, we estimate a spatial demand model in which category-specific store counts determine both origin trip generation and destination choice. The planner maximizes a trip-weighted logsum objective that values trip generation and access to retail destinations, subject to local vacancy capacity and limits on additions by category. We characterize complementarity and substitution by decomposing interactions into directed flow effects and competition for demand from shared origins. A transfer-search heuristic exploits the location-level constraint structure, while a concave lifting yields global upper bounds that certify allocation quality. Our empirical study combines approximately 112 million shopping and leisure trips with over 100,000 points of interest across 85 ZIP-code areas in Manhattan and Brooklyn. In the fitted model, 99.0% of combinations of eligible location–category pairs are complements for the planner’s objective at the computed allocation. The allocation favors restaurants and caf´es overall, with priorities varying across neighborhoods, and captures at least 99.993% of the maximum possible gain over constrained proportional filling. Matching its objective through uncapped expansion proportional to existing store counts would require 43.3% more store additions. These findings show how mobility-informed retail-mix planning can improve the use of existing commercial capacity.

title: Global Trade in Flux and the Way Forward for Korean Industry

detail.title: Global Trade in Flux and the Way Forward for Korean Industry
detail.abstract:
Shifts in US international strategy are abruptly reshaping the structure of goods trade between countries, while digital trade issues in services, especially those involving artificial intelligence (AI) platforms, finance, and data, are moving quickly.

The US trade deficit with China has fallen dramatically, yet the overall US trade deficit has actually grown, and a Great Reallocation is under way as the shares of some 20 other established major trading partners rise. With access to the US goods market now harder to come by, China’s vast export manufacturing output is rapidly eroding import markets in emerging countries and EU member states on the strength of rock-bottom prices, threatening the position of Korean industry.

In digital trade, the regulation of Big Tech platforms by the EU and other major economies is in sharp conflict with the US government’s determination to rein that regulation in. Korea’s rules on data transfer and personal information protection, and its financial regulation, including the rules on payments and settlement, are structured much like Europe’s, so Korea and the US can be expected to remain at odds in future tariff and investment negotiations.

Korea should concentrate its capabilities on strengthening the competitiveness of its advanced semiconductor industry, fundamentally improving the cost competitiveness of its industries, and raising its share of markets in emerging countries.

title: ODA in Retreat: Global Aid Cuts and Reshaping Development Cooperation

detail.abstract:
Preliminary data released by the OECD in April 2026 confirmed that official development assistance (ODA) from members of its Development Assistance Committee (DAC) fell 23.1 percent in 2025 to USD 174.3 billion, the steepest decline since records began.

The contraction stems not only from volatile items such as humanitarian aid and in-donor refugee costs but also from a retreat in the core of development cooperation, including development programs. It is also highly concentrated: the five largest donors account for 95.7 percent of the total decline, and the United States alone for 75.1 percent. At the same time, it marks a structural shift, with deep cuts to grants and to support for the UN alongside growth in private sector instruments (PSI) and in support for multilateral development banks.

The policy realignments of major donors point the same way. Through its development policy reform, Germany has made economic cooperation that reflects its own industrial structure one of four overarching goals; the United States has dismantled the US Agency for International Development (USAID) while sharply expanding the authority and resources of the US International Development Finance Corporation (DFC); and Japan is strengthening offer-type cooperation and security-focused cooperation.

South Korea occupies a distinctive position in this landscape. Its ODA declined only modestly in 2025 and its budget request for 2027 rebounded, but the number of projects has fallen sharply, leaving fewer and larger projects, while the shares going to health and to low-income countries have actually risen. This paper proposes three tasks for restructuring Korea’s development cooperation: putting a Korean model of development finance on an institutional footing, building the foundations for implementing proposal-based ODA, and strategically staking out a position in the gaps left by the withdrawal of major donors.

detail.abstract: The rapid adoption of artificial intelligence has fundamentally altered organizational decision-making. Algorithms increasingly provide initial recommendations, leaving human employees to verify their outputs and make final decisions. This shift raises a critical question: how should organizations motivate costly verification when employees can instead rely on readily available algorithmic advice? We study a principal-agent model of delegated forecasting in which an agent observes an algorithmic forecast and decides whether to acquire a costly human signal. We characterize the optimal contract and the resulting acquisition and forecasting strategies. Under symmetric predictive losses, it can be optimal to reward a false positive or a false negative, and sometimes to reward only mistakes. Algorithmic access can also improve or worsen accuracy relative to a human-only setting, as it can crowd out human verification or enable selective acquisition that would otherwise not occur. When the principal faces asymmetric predictive losses, rewarding mistakes can instead discourage verification and shift forecasts away from the more costly mistake. Our findings show that reward policies should account for both the operational consequences of forecasts and what they reveal about otherwise unobservable verification effort.

detail.abstract:
This volume represents the second collaborative publication produced under the KIET–ISID partnership, which seeks to promote policy dialogue and strengthen economic and industrial cooperation between Korea and India. While the previous volume, Reimagining India–Korea Economic Partnership: Pathways to Deepen Integration, focused primarily on identifying pathways to deepen economic integration between Korea and India, the present volume explores how the bilateral partnership can evolve toward a more comprehensive framework of industrial collaboration in response to changing global economic and geopolitical conditions.


The first part of the volume explores the evolving Korea–India economic partnership in the context of changing global economic conditions. The chapters examine foreign direct investment trends, emerging geopolitical challenges, and the implications of recent changes in the international economic order for bilateral cooperation.

The second part focuses on labor-intensive industries and digital transformation. These chapters discuss opportunities for cooperation in employment-intensive manufacturing sectors, SME development, and emerging digital technologies that can contribute to inclusive growth and industrial upgrading..

The third part examines strategic industries that are expected to play an increasingly important role in the future of Korea–India cooperation. Particular attention is given to sectors such as shipbuilding and steel, where complementarities between the two economies create opportunities for long-term industrial collaboration.

We hope that this volume will contribute to a deeper understanding of the opportunities and challenges facing Korea–India relations and serve as a useful reference for policymakers, researchers, industry stakeholders, and all those interested in advancing a stronger and more resilient Korea–India partnership.

detail.abstract: Existing end-to-end methods for contextual newsvendor problems fall into three widely separated regimes in the approximation landscape: global linear rules, local-constant kernel rules, and black-box neural policies. We introduce kernel polynomial quantile regression (KPQR), the missing intermediate family of local polynomial prescriptions. KPQR strictly generalizes Ban and Rudin (2019)'s Linear ERM and Kernel Optimization as its degree-one and degree-zero special cases, leverages local smoothness through a suitably chosen polynomial degree, and matches, up to logarithmic factors, the minimax optimal excess risk rates established for deep neural newsvendor policies (Han et al. 2026), both contextwise and globally. We further equip KPQR with a holdout selector that adapts to unknown smoothness. By incorporating the semicompeting censored quantile (SCQ) loss, we extend KPQR to censored demand while retaining the same polynomial excess risk rate. Our simulation studies support the theoretical guarantees. Finally, we apply KPQR to a real world fresh retail dataset for daily replenishment, where it consistently outperforms benchmark policies across all product categories and critical ratios.

detail.abstract:
A shrinking school-age population and the preference for universities in the Seoul Capital Area (SCA) are together rapidly weakening the ability of regional universities to fill their places and the foundations for developing local talent. The study warns that this could set off a vicious cycle in which a shrinking talent pool weakens industrial competitiveness and reduces jobs, job losses drive people out of the regions, and population outflow further erodes the competitiveness of regional universities. Workforce development outcomes also vary among regional universities. Until fairly recently, flagship national universities achieved outcomes broadly similar to those of SCA universities and had accumulated foundations for teaching and research. Recently, however, signs of weakening competitiveness have emerged, including declining admission competition ratios and employer reputation, which call for a preemptive response before those foundations erode further.

Completing the hub development strategy of balanced development policy depends above all on building a system, centered on flagship national universities, that develops talent in the regions to meet the needs of growth industries and keeps that talent there. Each region’s flagship national university should be developed into a core hub for talent development, research and development, and industry-academia collaboration, and should spread its results across the wider region through links with non-flagship universities, firms, and research institutes. Support for regional universities, likewise, needs to move away from scattered support for individual institutions toward a system that extends the capabilities of flagship national universities across the wider region.

Existing university support programs and R&D programs should also be linked and reorganized to fit talent development systems for each wider region, centered on flagship national universities, and tied to the workforce needs of each region’s growth industries.

detail.abstract:
Background and Problem: One of the most complex cognitive challenges for a coach during a session is managing the “present moment” and ensuring clarity in the “next facilitative move.” This involves discerning which observational framework to apply to the phenomenon at hand, identifying deviations from the session agreement, and determining when to pause the exploration. The “Tree of Life” metaphor, originating from collective narrative work with vulnerable populations (Ncube, 2006), has recently been adapted into individual coaching. However, transferring this tool without clear theoretical foundations and transparent boundaries is risky, potentially leading to the imposition of irrelevant hypotheses or unintentional slippage into clinical therapy.

Objective: To conduct a four-level genealogy of this metaphor’s transfer—from indigenous and archetypal roots to narrative redesign and its adaptation in coaching—to define the legitimate limits of its claims and provide clear decision-making rules through two structured frameworks: ROOTED and SEEDED.

Methodology: A tripartite conceptual analysis (Narrative Coaching, ACT in coaching, and Gestalt) is employed, justifying the three foundations of “language and narrative,” “cognitive awareness and acceptance,” and “embodied and phenomenological experience in the moment.” This is accompanied by an empirical-operational scenario presented across two sessions, alongside a matrix of indicators reflecting client agency and clarity.

Findings: The components of the Tree of Life metaphor must remain solely within the “conversational and reflective space” and should not be reduced to indicators of psychological assessment. Conflicts between existing interpretations of these signs are resolved by establishing a reference version. The two proposed frameworks advance different logics: ROOTED focuses on “stabilizing and anchoring resources before broad exploration,” while SEEDED is designed for “seeding, conducting limited behavioral experiments, and assessing acceptance.”

Conclusion: The proposed frameworks are structured design hypotheses that prepare the ground for future empirical research. By establishing limits of practice, this study provides a methodical guide for coaches to prevent straying from ICF core competencies.

detail.abstract: Apartheid era until today. We argue that South Africa’s position in the US-led international financial architecture is characterised by contradictions. As a BRICS member, South Africa appears to be among the key contestants of dollar hegemony. Yet it has been and remains deeply embedded in Anglo-Saxon financial capitalism, while acting as a regional financial hegemon that has established the rand as a regional key currency in Southern Africa. Drawing on the Global Credit View, we conceptualise South Africa’s financial system as a web of interlocking balance sheets that goes beyond the ‘triple coincidence’ of monetary, political, and economic area. We trace its integration into the Offshore Dollar System across three stages. During Apartheid, South Africa oscillated between integration to support its Minerals-Energy Complex and ringfencing, both voluntary to prevent capital flight and involuntary due to international sanctions. After 1994, liberalisation enabled South African balance sheets to accumulate foreign assets on a large scale. The 2001 currency crisis led the central bank to self-insure through large dollar reserves. Since joining the BRICS in 2010, South Africa has used its contradictory position to play the United States and China against each other while expanding its regional hegemony, for instance through the SADC-RTGS, a cross-border payment system operated by the South African Reserve Bank. We show that subordination in the Offshore Dollar System applies unevenly across the country’s balance sheets: the treasury has largely avoided foreign-currency debt, whereas some private balance sheets—largely associated with the historically white and now increasingly multi-racial elite—are deeply integrated and benefit from that integration. We posit that remaining connected to the Offshore Dollar System has been a structural imperative across very different political regimes. In consequence, South Africa is at once subordinated and subordinating. These contradictions are rooted in Apartheid-era balance sheet configurations that continue to shape the present.

detail.abstract: Annotation. This study provides a rigorous exploration of strategic governance within law enforcement frameworks, examined through the prism of global legal benchmarks and their transformative effect on public security architectures. It is posited that under the exigencies of globalization, law enforcement operations have transcended localized regulation, necessitating the institutionalization of strategic paradigms that align with the core tenets of the Rule of Law, transparency, and Good Governance. Central to this discourse is the conceptualization of leadership as the primary agent for discharging a state's international obligations, particularly in the realms of fundamental human rights preservation and the mitigation of transnational criminal threats. The research delineates the specific mechanisms through which executive command synchronizes internal administrative workflows with the normative mandates of global institutions, including the UN, the Council of Europe, Interpol, and Europol. The analysis demonstrates that strategic stewardship acts as the fundamental determinant in the paradigm shift from archaic punitive methodologies to a service-oriented model-a transition regarded as a cornerstone of contemporary international security law. Furthermore, the paper establishes that the efficacy of public security is inextricably linked to the executive's capacity to embed deontological standards and ethical protocols into the organizational fabric. The study concludes with the proposal of a bi-vector strategic model, which harmonizes the imperatives of national sovereignty with the mandates of the global legal regime for human rights protection. Finally, pragmatic recommendations are articulated to recalibrate strategic planning within the Ukrainian security apparatus, aligning it with the trajectory of European integration and comprehensive security sector reform.

detail.abstract: This paper develops a common analytical framework for firms, subnational governments, states and international organizations around one question: after contractual, hierarchical and status-based arrangements have been exhausted, who bears the terminal residual of joint consequences? Organizations create joint capabilities and, with them, consequences that the relations forming them cannot themselves bear. We define this terminal residual relative to a boundary fixed in advance, and distinguish three responsibility arrangements by where the residual falls by default: with a position integrated into the whole organization (upward-pooled), with contracting parties under bounded guarantees (contractual), or with local holders through status, possession or dependence (fixed). Two explanatory variables, effective external exit capacity and divisibility of consequences, organize a set of propositions. The testable propositions are paired with observations that would count against them; one problem concerning the formation of an integrated top is left explicitly open. We also propose a method for describing large organizations on five observable dimensions and illustrate it with materials from China, the United States and India. The cases are selected to illustrate different kinds of evidence, not to represent a wider population. The paper offers a framework and a research design. It does not report a test.

detail.abstract:
Federal evidence law protects confidences between lawyers and clients, between spouses, and between psychotherapists and patients. It does not extend the same protection to the mediation room. No federal privilege covers mediation communications: Rule 408 excludes them for limited purposes while leaving them discoverable, and admissible for others; the Uniform Mediation Act governs in only a minority of states; and in the three decades since federal district courts began recognizing a common-law mediation privilege, no court of appeals has followed. The consequence is a confidentiality regime that varies by state and procedural posture—for a process that federal courts order parties into every day, on an explicit assurance of confidentiality that federal law does not back.

This Article proposes Federal Rule of Evidence 503—Mediation Privilege. The proposal is less novel than it sounds. Congress contemplated national ADR-confidentiality rules in 1998 and directed the district courts to improvise by local rule only “until such time” as those rules arrived; the number 503 has been vacant since 1975, when Congress declined to enact the Advisory Committee’s privilege rules; and Rule 502 demonstrated in 2008 that the rulemaking process and Congress can together add a confidentiality rule to Article V when practice demands one. Drawing on state experimentation, the mixed reception of the Uniform Mediation Act, and the statutory regimes of the European Union, Singapore, and Hong Kong, the Article supplies what the debate has lacked: a complete rule text—definitions, holders, waiver, and calibrated exceptions—ready for the machinery Congress built and left waiting.

detail.abstract: This paper analyzes delegation from humans to AI by asking what should be specified in advance, which decisions should remain with humans, and which tasks should be assigned to AI. Building on the analysis of ex ante specification, authority allocation, and information transmission in contract theory and organizational economics, it formulates these issues as a problem of instruction design. An instruction is defined as complete if the candidate intents consistent with the instruction and shared context imply the same set of permissible actions in every relevant situation, and as incomplete otherwise. Even under an incomplete instruction, missing information about intent causes no loss if a common optimal action exists. A model with a binary decision criterion compares direct performance by a human, delegation to AI under complete instructions, and delegation to AI combining incomplete instructions with consultation on individual cases. A common attention constraint on human execution, instruction preparation, and responses to consultations jointly determines task assignment and the division of decision making within each task. Holding fixed an incomplete-instruction regime for a given task type, a higher shadow price of attention weakly reduces consultation, but need not induce a shift toward complete instructions because their preparation also requires time. The paper further analyzes a setting in which the same criterion persists and answers can be remembered, deriving the future value of consultation and the choice of ex ante specification. Using general principles of the value of information, it presents a limited theoretical model that makes human involvement through instruction, consultation, and execution comparable.

detail.abstract: We study how credit markets transmit overrides of local regulatory authority, exploiting U.S. state laws that preempt local regulation of natural gas. Combining a novel gas-dependence measure from SME energy audits with SBA loan data, we find that preemption raises loan volumes and lowers interest rates for gas-dependent borrowers, and reduces bunching of loans below SBA guarantee-fee thresholds. Lenders respond only to enacted laws, not to local bans, which can be overridden or overturned, consistent with lenders pricing the durability of future regulation. Employment in gas-dependent industries and industrial gas consumption also rise, suggesting that finance amplifies preemption into deeper carbon lock-in.

detail.abstract: Organizations increasingly use monitoring technologies to govern conduct and improve workplace safety. Under performance pressure, workers may take actions that advance their own or their team's interests while exposing others to injury. We examine whether technology-enabled inspection can restrain such conduct and reduce injuries. We study the staggered introduction of the Video Assistant Referee (VAR) across the Big Five European football leagues. VAR uses replay-assisted inspection to reassess consequential decisions while leaving incentives to compete intact. Difference-indifferences and event-study analyses of team-season, team-match, and player-match data from 2014/15 to 2021/22 yield a main estimate of approximately 27% fewer total injuries per team-season. We propose selective behavioral restraint as a core mechanism. Review can remove benefits obtained through misconduct, while clearer evidence and public attribution can raise the moral and reputational costs of violating standards of conduct. Aggressive and unsporting conduct, which is positively associated with injuries to opponents, declines after VAR adoption, whereas verbal dissent and abuse increase. Player-level analyses further show that lower injury risk is accompanied by reductions in some productive contributions. The findings connect inspection design to the prevention of injury risks imposed by others' pursuit of performance. For operations managers, the challenge is to restrain conduct that puts others at risk while accounting for the productive activities affected by that restraint.
